rv.q: There are more narrative twists than are necessary – all the new things we learn about these characters begin to feel slightly silly.
The Girl Who Fell resists the need for a perfect ending and is more powerful for it.
The result is a believable and heartfelt account of a contemporary tragedy.

cn.t: Sarah Rutherford's suicide-aftermath drama earns mixed-to-positive reviews for its nimble dialogue and unabashed approach to grief, though reactions vary on its tonal balance.
